text.p: Harnischfeger Industries Inc extended on Friday its cash tender offer for machine tool maker Giddings & Lewis Inc so it can weigh a rival bid by Germany's Thyssen AG..
Harnischfeger, which launched its $19-a-share cash tender offer for Giddings & Lewis in April, said it would extend the bid until June 20. The offer was previously scheduled to expire June 13.
Harnischfeger also said about 5,961,590 Giddings shares had been tendered and not withdrawn as of June 12 for its offer. Giddings has about 33.2 million shares outstanding.

Fond du Lac, Wis.,-based Giddings, which rejected Harnischfeger's offer as inadequate in May, announced Thursday it agreed to be acquired by Thyssen for $21 per share, or $675 million, plus assumed debt.
In its statement issued Friday, Harnischfeger reiterated that it would walk away from its Giddings offer if it "is satisfied that Thyssen's offer is bona fide."
Earlier, a spokesman for Harnischfeger said that, while the company viewed Giddings as a way to gain a foothold in the industrial products and services business, it has other options.
"We are very committed to the industrial products and services strategy," said David Brukardt, a spokesman for Milwaukee-based Harnischfeger.
"That doesn't necessarily mean we would have to do that with a machine tool maker."
